cells.tense: Right now you've got your hand on the work and you're building it on purpose, one piece at a time.
cells.ask: Let one person who's already good at this see the unfinished work, and take what they hand back as material rather than a verdict — it feeds the next piece.
cells.core:
There's something in front of you that didn't exist before, and you're the one raising it. Not by force — by knowing what goes where and being willing to keep going back to it. A rough frame becomes a room because you stayed with it.

You're spending time in this alone, and the solitude is holding rather than hiding. When you come back to people, what you built is more solid for it. The next thing asking for your hand isn't more certainty — it's someone else's read on what you're making, and letting that sharpen the work instead of stopping it.
cells.sheetLine: You're building it on purpose, and staying with it is what makes it hold.
cells.verb: building something new out of what the clearing left behind
cells.place: at the point where you decide which way this goes

cells.tense: You keep building ahead of where the work actually is, bracing for a version of this that hasn't been raised yet.
cells.ask: Go back to one person this is for and ask what they actually need from it — let that answer, not your version of the end, set the pace for a while.
cells.core:
The original draw was to raise one honest thing, and somewhere along the way the raising became a race to finish something no one asked you to finish yet. Every session gets measured against how far it's got, and the work keeps failing that test because the test moves. The structure stops being yours and starts being a defense.

What this looks like when it's right: you're deep in the making, and the direction comes from what the thing keeps asking for rather than from a picture of the end. Slow is not a problem there. The next step isn't more planning — it's turning to whoever this was always for and letting their actual need pull, so the work can walk instead of sprint.
cells.sheetLine: You're building to finish rather than building to build, and the finish line keeps moving.

cells.tense: The clearing already happened, and you're still standing past it, planning what to raise without raising it.
cells.ask: Say what this is and what it's for, out loud, to one person — not as an idea to be approved, just as something that exists — and let that be the first stone of it.
cells.core:
The old thing came down, and the ground is clean, and for a while now the decision about what to build has been waiting. You know what it should be. You've known. It stays as a plan because a plan can't be judged, and it doesn't get built because the saying would have to come first. Nothing is wrong with the work — the pen just hasn't touched the page.

Building at its plainest: a frame goes up, materials arrive, the shape becomes something other people can walk into. That's available to you today and not before, because the clearing is behind you. Take one thing that's been a plan in your head and speak it as something you're doing. That's not a push — it's just the first move of the thing you already chose.
cells.sheetLine: The ground's already cleared. You've just been standing on it.

cells.tense: You're making things and setting them where you think they should go, without having claimed the call as yours.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you've been treating as what the work wanted, and name it as your own — this direction, taken by you — then let that ownership steer the next decision.
cells.core:
There's direction in what you're doing, plenty of it — calls made, lines drawn, one option taken over another, and it's been reading as the project's momentum rather than your decision. So the direction keeps happening without anyone holding it, and every so often you turn up somewhere you didn't quite choose. The built thing gets your hands and not your name.

When it's going right, the aim comes out of what you're genuinely drawn to — the work bends toward what you actually care about, and you can point to the moment you turned it that way. The correction here is smaller and older than a bigger commitment: notice one time you were moved to take this route, and own that as the reason.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this. You just haven't signed for it.
